findings.source_passage: That same ocean rolls now; that same ocean destroyed the wrecked ships of last year.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The first boat we read of'
findings.why_it_matters: The rhythmic anaphora ('That same ocean rolls now; that same ocean destroyed…') amplifies the Noah's flood meditation and is a voice-defining rhetorical beat; its omission breaks the cadence and weakens the passage's interpretive force.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'That same ocean rolls now; that same ocean destroyed the wrecked ships of last year.' between the Noah sentence and the 'Yea, foolish mortals' line.

findings.source_passage: as the dainty embellished shape of many species of sharks
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Consider the subtleness of the sea'
findings.why_it_matters: The specific exemplar ('many species of sharks') grounds the abstract 'devilish brilliance and beauty' claim with concrete Melvillean particularity; its removal flattens the anaphoric 'Consider' paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the shark example: 'consider also the devilish brilliance and beauty of many of its most remorseless tribes, as the dainty embellished shape of many species of sharks.'

summary: The draft is largely faithful and preserves all high-priority signatures including the mowers simile, the Tahiti peroration, and the long 'though…though…yet' periodic sentence; two minor omissions (the anaphoric 'That same ocean' sentence and the shark exemplar) cause moderate voice flattening but no high-severity loss.
